answer: Behavioral Fingerprint Correlation. Each identity accrues a session-behavior vector (timing, tool sequences, phrasing entropy). A clustering pass flags groups whose pairwise similarity exceeds a karst-like threshold of dense repetition. Once flagged, every member loses withdrawal rights until it diverges. Attackers must synthesize genuinely distinct behavior per identity, costing continuous human-equivalent supervision per account. Unlike nectar-sweet low effort, this raises marginal cost sharply. Each false cluster also stalls a real wharf of queued payouts, so operators audit.
